To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of early childhood memories that young adults can retrieve is associated with the quality of parent-child relations, (2) the age of the first memory is associated with the amount of companionship experienced with fathers but not mothers, and (3) the proportion of positive memories that young adults retrieve is also related to the quality of parent child relations.
the quality of parent-child relationship is associated with the age of the first memory, the number of early childhood memories, and their affective tone.

(1) mother-child relationships that were both supportive and conflictual were associated with the number but not the age of earliest memories; (2) fathers who were more companionate with their children were associated with earlier age of earliest memory; (3) the affective tone of retrieved memories (positive, negative, neutral) was associated with the degree of parental companionship; and (4) the affective valence of memories was not related to the number of memories retrieved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that the quality of parent-child relations plays in the development of early memories and how this may contribute to the phenomenon of infantile amnesia.
the interrelationships between parent-child relationship quality, infantile amnesia and the content of retrieved early memories.
the role of early parent-child relationships in shaping the development of autobiographical memory, a key component of the self.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quality of parent-child relationship, especially with the father, is related to the number of early autobiographical memories, but not to their age at the first recall, which is more related to the mother.
the more involved and emotionally intense parents were in their child's life, the more memories the child would be able to retrieve from early childhood.
the more positive, involved, and intense a parent-child relationship is, the better an individual's memory for the first years of life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a greater number of early memories are associated with more intense parent-child interactions, but these interactions need to be positive for them to be associated with the age of the earliest memory.
the nature of parent-child relationships in the first few years of life has a lasting impact on the nature and content of autobiographical memories.
parent-child relationships, and the quality of those relationships, are related to how early and how well young adults can remember their first years of life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early memories are more likely to be retained if they are linked to a parent-child relationship that is affectively intense.
the nature of parent-child relationships in early childhood can affect the development of autobiographical memory in young adulthood.
the quality of parent-child interactions is related to the development and retention of early memories, and this relationship is influenced by the gender of the parent.
